steps.title: Import React, createContext, useContext, and useState
steps.instruction: Import React, createContext, useContext, and useState from 'react'.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in the necessary modules from the 'react' package.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing React and a hook
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.seedCode: // Import React, createContext, useContext, and useState from 'react' here
steps.expectedOutcome: The import statements are added at the top of the file, making React, createContext, useContext, and useState available for use.
successCriteria: React, createContext, useContext, and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported React, createContext, useContext, and useState. These are essential for creating and using context in React.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've imported some of the required modules, but not all. Make sure to import React, createContext, useContext, and useState from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The import statements are missing or incorrect. You need to import React, createContext, useContext, and useState from 'react'.

steps.title: Create CartContext using createContext
steps.instruction: Create a CartContext using React.createContext() and export it as a named export.
steps.hint: Call createContext from React to create a new context object. Use export const to make it available for import in other files.
steps.expectedOutcome: A CartContext object is created and exported, ready to be used as a context provider and consumer.
successCriteria: CartContext is created with React.createContext() and exported as a named export.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the CartContext. This context will serve as the central place to store and share cart data across components.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're using createContext from React and exporting the CartContext variable.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. You need to create a context object using React.createContext() and export it so other components can use it.

steps.title: Create CartProvider component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named CartProvider that accepts children as props.
steps.hint: Define a component that takes a children prop and returns something (you can return null for now).
steps.expectedOutcome: A CartProvider component is defined with children as a prop.
successCriteria: CartProvider is defined as a function that accepts children as a prop.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the CartProvider component. This will be the wrapper that provides cart state to your app.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you define a function named CartProvider that takes children as a prop.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component wasn't created correctly. Create a function named CartProvider that accepts children as a prop.

steps.title: Initialize cart state with useState
steps.instruction: Inside the CartProvider component, use the useState hook to create a state variable named 'cart' initialized as an empty array.
steps.hint: Call useState with an empty array [] as the initial value, and destructure the returned array into 'cart' and 'setCart'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: state for a list
const [items, setItems] = useState([]);
steps.expectedOutcome: The CartProvider component will have a cart state variable ready to hold cart items.
successCriteria: The CartProvider component contains a useState call that initializes 'cart' as an empty array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully initialized the cart state with an empty array.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using useState with an empty array [] as the initial value.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've used useState inside CartProvider to create a 'cart' state variable initialized to an empty array.

steps.title: Create addToCart function
steps.instruction: Inside the CartProvider component, define a function named addToCart that takes an item object as a parameter.
steps.hint: You can use either a function declaration or an arrow function. The function should be defined before the return statement.
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have an addToCart function defined inside the CartProvider component.
successCriteria: The addToCart function is defined with a single parameter named 'item'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the addToCart function. Next we'll implement what it should do.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the function is named exactly 'addToCart' and takes one parameter called 'item'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The addToCart function isn't defined correctly. Check that it's inside the CartProvider component and has the right name and parameter.

steps.title: Create removeFromCart function
steps.instruction: Inside the CartProvider component, define a function named removeFromCart that takes an item id as a parameter and removes that item from the cart state.
steps.hint: You can use the setCart function to update the state. Filter the current cart array to exclude the item with the matching id.
steps.expectedOutcome: The CartProvider component now contains a removeFromCart function that filters out items by id from the cart state.
successCriteria: A function named removeFromCart is defined inside CartProvider, takes an id parameter, and updates the cart state by removing the matching item.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the removeFromCart function. This will allow users to remove items from their cart.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your function is named removeFromCart, takes an id parameter, and properly updates the cart state using setCart.
steps.feedbackWrong: The removeFromCart function is not correctly defined. Check that it's inside CartProvider, has the right name and parameter, and updates the state by filtering the cart array.

steps.title: Create clearCart function
steps.instruction: Inside the CartProvider component, define a function named clearCart that sets the cart state to an empty array.
steps.hint: You can create a function that calls setCart with an empty array [].
steps.expectedOutcome: The clearCart function should be defined inside the CartProvider component and should reset the cart state to an empty array.
successCriteria: A function named clearCart is defined inside the CartProvider component and it sets the cart state to an empty array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the clearCart function that will reset the cart.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your clearCart function sets the cart state to an empty array.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've defined a function named clearCart inside the CartProvider component that sets the cart state to [].

steps.title: Prepare value object for CartContext.Provider
steps.instruction: Inside the CartProvider component, create a value object that contains the cart state and all three cart functions (addToCart, removeFromCart, clearCart).
steps.hint: Create a JavaScript object with properties for cart, addToCart, removeFromCart, and clearCart. Use the variable names you've already defined.
steps.expectedOutcome: A value object is created inside CartProvider, containing cart state and the three cart functions as properties.
successCriteria: A value object is defined with properties for cart, addToCart, removeFromCart, and clearCart.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the value object that will be provided to all components using the CartContext.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your value object includes all four properties: cart, addToCart, removeFromCart, and clearCart.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try creating a JavaScript object with properties for cart, addToCart, removeFromCart, and clearCart. Remember to use the variable names you've already defined.

steps.title: Wrap children with CartContext.Provider
steps.instruction: In your CartProvider component, return CartContext.Provider with the value object, wrapping the children prop.
steps.hint: Use the CartContext.Provider component and pass the value object as a prop. The children prop should be placed between the opening and closing tags.
steps.expectedOutcome: The CartProvider component returns CartContext.Provider with the value object, wrapping the children prop.
successCriteria: CartContext.Provider is returned with the value object and children prop wrapped inside.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully wrapped the children with CartContext.Provider, making the cart context available to all child components.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're returning CartContext.Provider with both the value prop and the children prop wrapped inside.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. Remember to return CartContext.Provider with the value object and wrap the children prop inside it.

steps.title: Create useCart custom hook
steps.instruction: Define and export a custom hook named 'useCart' that returns the value from useContext(CartContext).
steps.hint: Create a function that calls useContext with CartContext and returns its value. Remember to export it so other components can use it.
steps.expectedOutcome: A custom hook named useCart is defined and exported, which returns the value from useContext(CartContext).
successCriteria: The useCart hook is defined and exported, and it returns useContext(CartContext).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the useCart custom hook. This will make it easy for components to access the cart context.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your useCart hook returns the value from useContext(CartContext) and is exported.
steps.feedbackWrong: The useCart hook should be defined and exported, and it should return useContext(CartContext). Try again.

steps.title: Create ProductItem component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named ProductItem that accepts product data as props and returns a simple div with the product name.
steps.hint: Define a component that takes props as its parameter and returns JSX. You can access the product name via props.product.name.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a ProductItem component that can display product information.
successCriteria: ProductItem component is defined, accepts props, and returns JSX containing the product name.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the ProductItem component that will display product data.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started creating the ProductItem component, but make sure it accepts props and returns JSX with the product name.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ProductItem component isn't properly defined yet. Create a component that takes props and returns a div with the product name.

steps.title: Use useCart hook in ProductItem and add Add to Cart button
steps.instruction: Inside the ProductItem component, use the useCart hook to get the addToCart function, then add a button with an onClick handler that calls addToCart with the product object.
steps.hint: Call useCart() to get the addToCart function, then create a button element with onClick={() => addToCart(product)}.
steps.expectedOutcome: The ProductItem component will have access to the addToCart function via useCart, and an 'Add to Cart' button that adds the product to the cart when clicked.
successCriteria: useCart hook is called inside ProductItem
addToCart function is destructured from useCart
Button element with onClick handler is added
onClick calls addToCart with the product object
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully connected the ProductItem component to the cart context. The button will now add products to the cart when clicked.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're calling useCart() to get the addToCart function, and the button's onClick should call addToCart with the product.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's review: Inside ProductItem, call useCart() to get the addToCart function, then add a button with onClick={() => addToCart(product)}.
